paragraphs: Caution signal | You need to observe learning continuously, maintain classroom order, and protect students; when danger arises, first safeguard students under emergency procedures, stop dangerous activities, and report, without abandoning your post. Insufficient evidence: this round's NBS2025 industry / broad personnel-category wages and Hubei recruitment announcements did not establish a nationwide wage distribution for elementary school teachers in mainland China; industry averages and specific recruitment compensation cannot substitute for occupational medians, percentiles, or starting pay.

Responsibility assessment | Real fit comes from whether you can do three things within the same job: make teaching a reviewable cycle (design instruction around curriculum standards and learning needs, prepare materials, teach and practice, assess learning, record and adjust, producing reviewable lesson designs and learning records); manage classrooms and student safety (classroom behavior rules and procedures, student supervision and emergency responses, student information and privacy protection, and communication boundaries with parents and colleagues, following school systems and local rules); and accept definable job responsibilities (take responsibility for your teaching and records and report matters beyond your role or authority under school procedures). Test this through a verifiable experience—creating a lesson design and learning assessment record using an entirely fictional classroom scenario—rather than relying only on interest questionnaire conclusions.

Trial method | Use pathway V's fixed three responses and four scoring rules to submit four work samples: a 10-minute lesson plan, scoring and feedback, 45/54 recalculation, and boundaries for further observation; follow the seven-day plan. Use no real children or personal information; this cannot replace qualifications or evidence of real teaching performance.

Fit signals | O*NET 25-2021.00 work activities emphasize training and teaching others, interpreting information, establishing and maintaining relationships, organizing and planning work, and making decisions and solving problems. If you are willing to keep checking classroom design, student learning, and classroom management, remain patient amid frequent interpersonal contact and noise, and make teaching and records a reviewable cycle, these daily demands are closer to your working style; interest and personality tools only help design trials and cannot determine teacher qualifications, hiring, or performance.

Elementary school teachers, except special education, correspond to U.S. 25-2021.00. They teach elementary academic and social skills, design instruction, manage classrooms, observe and assess learning, and record feedback. U.S. 2025 median annual wage is 63,970 USD. Insufficient evidence: this round's NBS2025 industry / broad personnel-category wages and Hubei recruitment announcements did not establish a nationwide wage distribution for elementary school teachers in mainland China; industry averages and specific recruitment compensation cannot substitute for occupational medians, percentiles, or starting pay. Current U.S. national wages: 2025 median 63,970 USD/year; 2025 employment 1,419,300, 2025—2035 growth 0% (rounded, essentially unchanged), and average annual openings 87,500 (overall projections, not AI attribution). The gap in exact occupational wages for China remains; industry averages are broad references only.

entries: Work objects | Students and classes, curriculum standards and textbooks, teaching resources and classroom environments, assessment records, and parent communication form the basis of teaching within school systems and local rules.

Checkable outputs | Reviewable instructional designs and lesson plans, classroom activity and material preparation records, student learning and behavior observations, assessment and feedback records, and parent communication and referral records; results must be traceable to curriculum standards and evidence of learning needs.

Complete workflow | Check learning needs and curriculum standards → design and prepare learning activities → teach individuals and groups while maintaining classroom order → observe and assess learning → record, provide feedback, and adjust teaching.

paragraphs: Key judgments | O*NET work context reports: email, 100% daily; teamwork, 97% extremely important; constant contact with others, 89%; workweek, 97% over 40 hours; face-to-face discussions, 89% daily; public speaking, 85% daily; coordinating or leading others, 71% extremely important. Judgments rely on curriculum standards and learning evidence, classroom observations and assessment records, and student safety and privacy requirements. These are U.S. respondent distributions, not fixed Chinese requirements or inevitable hours for every teacher.

Environment and pace | Work mainly involves classroom teaching and class management: physical proximity, 95% very close; controlled indoor environment, 83% daily; noise or distraction, 54% daily; standing, 54% continually; conflict situations, 46% daily; dealing with unpleasant or angry people, 42% daily; decision frequency, 68% daily; responsibility for others' health and safety, 53% very high; time pressure, 43% at least weekly but not daily; decision freedom, 43% some freedom. Timetables, assessment cycles, and school–family communication drive the pace. All describe U.S. respondents' contexts.

Research inputs | Retain official interest code S; S100/A48/C46 is not an official SAC code. Job Zone4 is not a qualification threshold, and Bright Outlook does not mean positive growth. Current 2025 educational services share is 98%; elementary 25-2021 employment is 1,419,300, projected to reach 1,413,400 over 2025—2035, with rounded growth of 0% and O*NET average annual openings of 87,500 (not net new jobs); 99,400 belongs to the combined kindergarten and elementary group. 2025 annual wage percentiles are 47,960/57,710/63,970/81,450/104,340 USD/year; no official hourly wages are provided, so do not convert.

This work first checks objects (students and classes, curriculum standards and textbooks, teaching resources and classroom environments), inputs (learning needs and curriculum standards, teaching and assessment materials, student safety and privacy requirements, school systems), and deliverables (instructional designs and lesson plans, learning and behavior observations, assessment and feedback records, parent communication and referral records). Anything unverified remains pending verification; experience or intuition cannot replace learning evidence and institutional requirements.

Work cycle | Check learning needs / curriculum → define teaching tasks → teach, assess, and record → review and adjust. Stop dangerous activities first, safeguard students, and initiate emergency reporting under institutional rules; do not abandon students. When evidence is insufficient, pause affected evaluations or diagnoses, gather observations, and consult; ordinary classroom support continues within authority, rather than stopping all teaching.

Classification boundaries | This page's 25-2021.00 differs from specialized special education occupations; excluding that occupational category does not mean rejecting students in the classroom who need additional support. O*NET includes adapting materials / assistive facilities, while BLS describes collaboration and co-teaching between general and special education teachers; professional diagnosis and individualized support follow team arrangements and institutional rules.

Which interests, abilities, and working styles matter more for elementary school teachers, except special education? This page discusses fit through work samples and responsibility boundaries only, without using personality labels to replace judgments of teacher qualifications or performance.

Direct answer | Fit signals are willingness to keep checking learning needs, curriculum standards, and student outcomes, patience amid frequent interpersonal contact and noise, a reviewable cycle of teaching and records, and reporting student safety issues or needs beyond one's abilities under institutional rules, rather than personality labels. Interest and personality tools only help design trials, not determine teacher qualifications, hiring, or performance.

Positive signals | You can design and prepare instruction against curriculum standards and organize individual and group teaching; observe and record student learning and behavior and adjust accordingly; and clearly document classroom rules, safety points, and school–family communication.

Caution conditions | Risk signals include loss of classroom order or inadequate student safety supervision, insufficient learning assessment evidence, ignoring individual differences, improper student information handling, and missing parent communication records; difficulty with continual interpersonal contact, noise, and workweeks over 40 hours represents practical costs to weigh seriously.

Trial action | Check three responses using V inputs, score A4/B2/C1, and explain carrying and 45/54; submit lesson plan, feedback, recalculation, and boundary work samples, and cross-check through the seven-day plan. Use no real children and do not judge student ability or disorders from one problem.

Conclusion | Activity preferences are closer to Social (O*NET interest code S, including teaching and education, social service, and professional counseling); interest codes only help design trials, not determine teacher qualifications or performance.

Personality boundaries | This page has not verified the scales' predictive validity for elementary teacher performance; record V explanations, scoring, patient feedback, and revisions, without reaching hiring or performance conclusions from personality labels.

Conclusion | RIASEC or personality frameworks only help formulate questions; they cannot replace occupational teacher qualifications and licensing, student safety responsibilities, or evidence of actual teaching performance. No tool conclusion constitutes a hiring, authorization, or qualification judgment.

Student safety | Prevent hazards under school supervision and emergency assignments, protect students, and report; China's primary and secondary teacher code prohibits abandoning posts without regard for students. Stopping dangerous activities does not mean stopping student supervision.

Assessment boundaries | Teaching assessment requires learning evidence and review; V assesses only three fictional responses and does not diagnose ability or disorders. Excluding special education from the occupational classification does not exclude ordinary classroom support; address needs through school and professional-team collaboration.

Student information and privacy risk | Trigger: processing, sharing, or sending student grades, behavior, or family information beyond authorized scope. Consequence: may infringe student and family rights and violate rules. Controls: minimum-necessary use, restricted systems and scope, and retained handling records. Boundary: school systems and applicable laws determine information protection.

School–family and colleague communication risk | Trigger: missing parent communication records, inconsistent student evaluations, or statements beyond authority. Consequence: may cause misunderstanding and unclear responsibility. Controls: retain communication records, use facts and checkable evidence, and follow school processes for assessment and handling. Boundary: school systems determine external communication content and messaging.

Workload and psychological depletion risk | Trigger: overlapping timetables and assessment cycles, sustained workweeks over 40 hours, and intensive interpersonal contact. Consequence: may reduce teaching quality and deplete personal energy. Controls: prioritize work, preserve key teaching and recordkeeping steps, and request support under school systems when needed. Boundary: school systems determine workload and support arrangements.

Preparation and qualifications | U.S. public elementary teachers generally need a bachelor's degree and teacher preparation / practicum, plus state certification or licensing for the grade level taught; common requirements include background checks and exams, while state rules and alternative preparation routes vary. Private teachers generally need a bachelor's degree but usually not the same state license; do not interpret Job Zone4's general several years of experience as a universal teacher entry period.

Entry checks | U.S. public elementary teachers generally need a bachelor's degree and teacher preparation / practicum, plus state certification or licensing for the grade level taught; common requirements include background checks and exams, while state rules and alternative preparation routes vary. Private teachers generally need a bachelor's degree but usually not the same state license; do not interpret Job Zone4's general several years of experience as a universal teacher entry period. Article 11 of China's Teachers Law sets elementary qualification education at secondary normal school graduation or above; check qualification conditions and recognition under Articles 10/13 and employment under Article 17 separately; exams, recognition, and job requirements also require local checks. The Ministry of Education's 2026 recruitment notice requires the qualification certificate before employment formalities and checks education, Putonghua, and physical and mental conditions; this is not equivalent to U.S. state licensing.

The Ministry of Education's 2026 recruitment notice requires the qualification certificate before employment formalities and checks education, Putonghua, and physical and mental conditions; this is not equivalent to U.S. state licensing.

Qualification boundaries | Courses, certificates, or training do not automatically grant teacher qualifications, hiring, or independent classroom authority; education, qualification certificates, licenses, hiring, school authorization, and sign-off responsibility are different statuses, with specific requirements depending on location and employer.

Stage responsibilities | During entry and practicum stages, prepare lessons, assist classrooms, and keep records under an experienced teacher's guidance; after taking independent classes, independently design instruction around curriculum standards and class needs and accept teaching, assessment, and recordkeeping responsibilities.

Paper exercise V | Entirely fictional, designed and cross-checked only by adults, without real children. Fixed goal: explain carrying in the ones place for 28+17 and check the result; input A answers '8+7=15, write 5 in ones and carry 1 to tens, 2+1+1=4, so 45'; B answers '8+7=15, write 5 in ones, 2+1=3, so 35'; C answers '2+1=3, 8+7=15, join them as 315.' Simulated rules: V1 exchange every 10 ones for 1 ten; V2 assess only this response, without diagnosing student ability or disorders; V3 use only paper, pencils, and place-value grids, with no personal information. Task: write a 10-minute simulated explanation; score place alignment, ones calculation, carrying, and result checking at 0/1 each; give neutral feedback for the three responses and the next problem, 36+18; record which explanations still need later observation.

Reference answer | 28+17=45; A scores 4/4 across four items; B has correct place alignment / ones calculation but omits carrying and has a wrong result, scoring 2/4; C calculates both places separately but fails to combine place values correctly, omits carrying, and has a wrong result, scoring 1/4 (only 1 point for ones calculation). Feedback for B: exchange 15 ones for 1 ten and 5 ones, and add the exchanged 1 to tens; feedback for C: 15 is not simply appended; exchange for a ten using the place-value grid. 36+18=54: 6+8=14, ones 4, tens 3+1+1=5. Scoring follows V's simulated rules only and cannot establish real learning effects or student diagnoses. 10-minute schedule: goal 1, demonstration 3, three-card discussion 3, checking 36+18 for 2, review 1. Four work samples: goal / 10-minute lesson plan; A—C scoring and feedback table; place-value answers and recalculation table for both problems; simulated records and a checklist of further-observation / safety and information boundaries. Seven-day plan | 20—30 minutes daily: D1 read V inputs and write the goal; D2 draw place-value grids and recalculate 45/54; D3 score A4, B2, C1 against four items; D4 write neutral feedback and further-observation questions; D5 rehearse on paper with adults using 1+3+3+2+1 minutes; D6 ask a peer to cross-check only against V rules and retain errors such as missed carrying and revisions; D7 combine four work samples and check target-region qualifications, preparation, and recruitment announcements. Fictional scoring is not formal assessment; work samples grant no teacher qualification or independent teaching authority.

Transfer pathways | Before transitioning, list transferable abilities (instructional design and delivery, classroom management and student safety, learning assessment and records, communication with families and colleagues, and curriculum and resource selection), then identify qualifications and evidence of responsibility required for the new role; moving into education management, preschool or kindergarten teaching, teacher preparation, or higher education requires evidence of each role's education, qualifications, and job authorization.

risks.affected_roles: Elementary school teachers, except special education
risks.consequence: May cause student injuries and incidents involving liability.
risks.mitigation: Safeguard students and report under emergency assignments; abandoning posts without regard for students is prohibited.
risks.scenario: Inadequate student supervision during classes or activities, or missing emergency preparation.

risks.affected_roles: Elementary school teachers, except special education
risks.consequence: May cause inappropriate learning support and distorted progress records.
risks.mitigation: Gather observations and review affected assessments; give feedback only from response evidence, without diagnosing ability or disorders.
risks.scenario: Insufficient learning assessment evidence or teaching design mismatched to curriculum standards and learning needs.

risks.affected_roles: Elementary school teachers, except special education
risks.consequence: May infringe student and family rights and violate rules.
risks.mitigation: Use the minimum necessary, restrict systems and scope, and retain handling records.
risks.scenario: Processing, sharing, or sending student grades, behavior, or family information beyond authorized scope.

risks.affected_roles: Elementary school teachers, except special education
risks.consequence: May cause misunderstanding and unclear responsibility.
risks.mitigation: Retain communication records, use facts and checkable evidence, and follow school processes for assessment and handling.
risks.scenario: Missing parent communication records, inconsistent student evaluations, or statements beyond authority.

risks.affected_roles: Elementary school teachers, except special education
risks.consequence: May reduce teaching quality and deplete personal energy.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize work, preserve key teaching and recordkeeping steps, and request support under school systems when needed.
risks.scenario: Overlapping timetables and assessment cycles, sustained workweeks over 40 hours, and intensive interpersonal contact.

risks.affected_roles: Elementary school teachers, except special education
risks.consequence: May cross job and safety boundaries.
risks.mitigation: Stop dangerous activities or affected assessment / information-handling steps, maintain student supervision, report under institutional rules, and consult support teams.
risks.scenario: Continuing despite student safety risks, needs beyond one's abilities, or insufficient information security conditions.

subject.summary: Elementary teachers teach elementary academic and social skills, design instruction, manage classrooms, observe learning, and record feedback. First check target-region teacher qualifications and school requirements; use V's fictional responses to practice teaching and assessment. U.S. 2025 median annual wage is 63,970 USD; national occupational wage evidence for China is insufficient.
